upstream.implementation: C++17 header-oriented turn-taking engine using vendored miniaudio

source_observations: The upstream engine intentionally performs turn-taking without an LLM, ASR, or neural VAD; it uses acoustic/prosodic evidence and a cost policy, so it cannot understand the lexical content of German speech by itself.
The microphone is intended to remain active while the system speaks. Upstream combines echo-aware band evidence and NCC-derived evidence for barge-in instead of muting capture during playback.

Barge-in evidence is separated from intent: strong acoustic evidence alone is not allowed to immediately mint an interruption decision; duration/cost logic distinguishes a likely interruption from a short backchannel.

The policy explicitly states that its inherited pause prior is based on Swedish/English measurements and includes a calibration path from observed user pauses/gaps. Therefore German timing quality must be measured rather than inferred from language-independence of the DSP.
CMake gates Apple audio frameworks behind APPLE, which is compatible with a potentially portable core, but no Linux/clay-direct-dev build or runtime was observed in this audit.
The bundled TTS adapter hard-depends on macOS say plus afconvert. The upstream application is therefore not a drop-in Linux Frankenstein voice stack even if useful core modules compile elsewhere.

f2_transfer_candidates.role: candidate acoustic evidence lane below VoiceIntent/GWT
f2_transfer_candidates.reason: May improve open-speaker interruption detection when near-end speech is quieter than residual self-echo.
Separates real speech evidence from intent-to-take-floor, matching Frankenstein's observation-versus-intent boundary.
Offers an explicit way to replace inherited Swedish/English pause priors with local session evidence.
The upstream design tracks what audio was actually played/heard when an utterance is interrupted, conceptually aligned with Frankenstein's unheard-audio cancellation boundary.

rule-based response agent has no semantic dialogue value for Frankenstein cognition
Linux compile, ALSA/PipeWire device behavior, CPU cost, AEC stability, and real room ERLE are unmeasured on clay-direct-dev
upstream repository claims of live behavior remain upstream evidence until independently reproduced
hypothesis: A small extracted subset consisting of echo-aware barge-in evidence, backchannel/interruption arbitration, and gap/pause calibration could improve Frankenstein's open-speaker full-duplex robustness without replacing semantic turn control or GWT authority.
counterhypothesis: Frankenstein's existing PipeWire/ALSA/WebRTC/Silero and semantic turn-control path already captures the useful signal; adding another DSP/policy layer would duplicate mechanisms, complicate calibration, and fail to improve German room metrics.
